label: Is your child also struggling in academics?
As a parent, do you also feel that my child is smart, but his marks are low?
He can read but doesn't understand what he has read.
He knows the answer at home but forgets in exam, or does not know how to write it down.
Hi, this is Anjali Rawat. I'm a clinical psychologist.
These concerns may point out to the specific learning disability, and it has nothing to do with intelligence.
These signs can appear as early as 6 to 8 years, like mixing up of alphabets b and d, slow handwriting,
spelling the same words differently each time, messy handwriting despite having several attempts, trouble with numbers and avoiding homework.
And these are not because they aren't bright, but because their brain works differently.
Many of the children do best when their learning is broken down into small and specific steps.
Don't label your child. Get an assessment.
A formal one is usually done once the schooling begins, but support can start much earlier.
With early help, your child can do wonders.
Your child is not lazy. He just learns differently.
If you notice the signs, please reach out to us at The Cub, as we are here to help you.
